title: Watch an attribute change
summary: observedAttributes names the attributes a custom element watches.
introduction: observedAttributes names the attributes a custom element watches. Your task: Change the last score value to 9.
learningObjectives: Change the last score value to 9.
Explain the example for watch an attribute change

blocks.text: observedAttributes names the attributes a custom element watches. attributeChangedCallback runs when one of those values changes.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<score-note score="2"></score-note>
<script>
  class ScoreNote extends HTMLElement {
    static observedAttributes = ["score"];
    attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) { this.textContent = "Score: " + newValue; }
  }
  customElements.define("score-note", ScoreNote);
  document.querySelector("score-note").setAttribute("score", "5");
</script>
blocks.title: Watch an attribute change

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`observedAttributes` lists the attribute names that should trigger `attributeChangedCallback`.

blocks.text: The component ends with Score: 5. Its watched score attribute causes the update.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Only listed attributes trigger this callback. Do not set the same attribute endlessly from its own callback.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change the last score value to 9.
